questions.question: The S.I. base unit of length is the:
questions.explanation: The S.I. base unit of length is the metre (m). Kilogram is mass, second is time, and ampere is electric current.

questions.question: The S.I. base unit of mass is the:
questions.explanation: The S.I. base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg). Gram and pound are non-SI, newton is force.

questions.question: The S.I. base unit of time is the:
questions.explanation: The S.I. base unit of time is the second (s). Minute, hour, and day are non-SI units.

questions.question: The S.I. base unit of electric current is the:
questions.explanation: The S.I. base unit of electric current is the ampere (A). Volt is potential difference, ohm is resistance, coulomb is charge.

questions.question: The S.I. base unit of thermodynamic temperature is the:
questions.explanation: The S.I. base unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin (K). Celsius and Fahrenheit are non-SI scales.

questions.question: The S.I. base unit of amount of substance is the:
questions.explanation: The S.I. base unit of amount of substance is the mole (mol). Candela is luminous intensity, kelvin is temperature, kilogram is mass.

questions.question: The S.I. base unit of luminous intensity is the:
questions.explanation: The S.I. base unit of luminous intensity is the candela (cd). Lumen and lux are derived photometric units, watt is power.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an S.I. base unit?
questions.explanation: The newton (N) is a derived S.I. unit (force), not a base unit. Metre, kilogram, and second are base units.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of force is the:
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). Joule is energy, watt is power, pascal is pressure.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of pressure is the:
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa). Newton is force, joule is energy, watt is power.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of energy is the:
questions.explanation: Energy is measured in joules (J). Watt is power, newton is force, pascal is pressure.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of power is the:
questions.explanation: Power is measured in watts (W). Joule is energy, newton is force, hertz is frequency.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of frequency is the:
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), which is one cycle per second.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of electric charge is the:
questions.explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs (C). Ampere is current, volt is potential difference, ohm is resistance.

questions.question: The prefix kilo means:
questions.explanation: The prefix kilo means 103 (one thousand).

questions.question: The prefix milli means:
questions.explanation: The prefix milli means 10-3 (one thousandth).

questions.question: The prefix micro means:
questions.explanation: The prefix micro means 10-6 (one millionth).

questions.question: The prefix mega means:
questions.explanation: The prefix mega means 106 (one million).

questions.question: The prefix giga means:
questions.explanation: The prefix giga means 109 (one billion).

questions.question: The prefix nano means:
questions.explanation: The prefix nano means 10-9 (one billionth).

questions.question: 1 kilometre is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 kilometre = 1000 metres.

questions.question: 1 centimetre is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 centimetre = 0.01 metres (10-2 m).

questions.question: 1 millimetre is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 millimetre = 0.001 metres (10-3 m).

questions.question: 1 micrometre is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 micrometre = 10-6 metres.

questions.question: 1 nanometre is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 nanometre = 10-9 metres.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity = displacement / time, so its dimension is LT-1.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration = velocity / time, so its dimension is LT-2.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of force is:
questions.explanation: Force = mass × acceleration, so its dimension is MLT-2.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of work is:
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance, so its dimension is ML2T-2.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of power is:
questions.explanation: Power = work / time, so its dimension is ML2T-3.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of pressure is:
questions.explanation: Pressure = force / area, so its dimension is ML-1T-2.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of density is:
questions.explanation: Density = mass / volume, so its dimension is ML-3.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of area is:
questions.explanation: Area = length × length, so its dimension is L2.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of volume is:
questions.explanation: Volume = length × length × length, so its dimension is L3.

questions.question: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring the diameter of a thin wire?
questions.explanation: A micrometer screw gauge has a very small least count (0.01 mm) and is best for measuring the diameter of a thin wire.

questions.question: The least count of a vernier caliper is usually:
questions.explanation: A vernier caliper typically has a least count of 0.01 cm (0.1 mm).

questions.question: The least count of a micrometer screw gauge is usually:
questions.explanation: A micrometer screw gauge typically has a least count of 0.01 mm.

questions.question: The least count of a metre rule is usually:
questions.explanation: A metre rule typically has a least count of 0.1 cm (1 mm).

questions.question: Zero error in a vernier caliper occurs when:
options: The jaws are closed and the zero marks do not coincide
questions.explanation: Zero error occurs when the jaws are closed but the zero mark of the vernier does not coincide with the zero mark of the main scale.

questions.question: To correct for a positive zero error, the zero error is:
questions.explanation: For a positive zero error, the error is subtracted from the observed reading to get the correct value.

questions.question: The number 0.00340 has how many significant figures?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant. The digits 3, 4, and the trailing zero after the decimal are significant, so there are 3 significant figures.

questions.question: The number 0.00580 has how many significant figures?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant. The digits 5, 8, and the trailing zero after the decimal are significant, so there are 3 significant figures.

questions.question: Rounding 4.567 to two decimal places gives:
questions.explanation: The third decimal digit is 7, so we round up the second decimal digit from 6 to 7, giving 4.57.

questions.question: The number 0.00045 expressed in scientific notation is:
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point 4 places to the right to get 4.5, so 0.00045 = 4.5 × 10-4.

questions.question: The number 3.0 × 10<sup>4</sup> has how many significant figures?
questions.explanation: In scientific notation, all digits in the coefficient are significant. The coefficient 3.0 has 2 significant figures.

questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Mass is a scalar quantity because it has magnitude only. Velocity, force, and displacement are vectors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector quantity because it has both magnitude and direction. Speed, distance, and mass are scalars.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of the gravitational constant G is:
questions.explanation: From F = G m1m2/r2, G = Fr2/(m1m2). Its dimension is M-1L3T-2.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of Planck's constant h is:
questions.explanation: From E = hf, h = E/f. Energy has dimension ML2T-2 and frequency has T-1, so h has dimension ML2T-1.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of magnetic flux density is the:
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla (T). Weber is magnetic flux, henry is inductance, farad is capacitance.
